excerpt: ui: share conversations to Hugging Face datasets as agent traces (#32608) ui: add @ggml-org/llama-huggingface, a Hugging Face account as a package A package in ui/lib that gives an app running in the browser, with no server of its own, a Hugging Face account. Its plain entry holds "Sign in with Hugging Face" (OAuth with PKCE and dynamic client registration) and the Hub calls: who the account is, its datasets, and committing a trace file to one. Its Svelte entry holds the account as state (HfAccount) and the components that show it, built on Llama UI: the account panel and the dialog that shares a trace. It knows no app: the app says who it is and hands over what to share. Llama Chat compiles it from source, like the other packages, so the llama-server image builds (.devops) and the asset staging (scripts/ui-assets.cmake) copy its sources next to the other packages'. CI checks and tests it. Assisted-by: Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium) ui: share conversations to Hugging Face datasets as agent traces A conversation's menu and each message get a Share action. It uploads the conversation, or the branch up to that message, to a Hugging Face dataset as a JSONL trace, which the Hub shows in its trace viewer. The sign-in is part of the share: the dialog (@ggml-org/llama-huggingface) asks for it with "Sign in with Hugging Face" (contribute-repos: the app creates datasets and writes only to the ones it created) or with a pasted access token. It then shows the datasets the account can add to as tiles, with a tile to create a new one (public unless the private option is ticked); with none to add to, it asks for the name of a new dataset. A pasted token reaches every dataset of the account; a sign-in reaches the ones this browser shared to. Once shared, the dialog shows the trace as a file with the first messages of the conversation fading out below it, and every action in one place at the bottom right.
